title: Old Testament Adventures Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of the Old Testament heroes from Noah to David!

questions.question: What did God tell Noah to build?
questions.explanation: God told Noah to build an ark (a large boat) to save his family and the animals from the great flood (Genesis 6:14).

questions.question: What was God's sign of His promise to never flood the whole earth again?
questions.explanation: God put a rainbow in the sky as a sign of His covenant promise to never flood the whole earth again (Genesis 9:13).

questions.question: What special promise did God make to Abraham?
options: He would be the strongest man
He would live forever on earth
He would be the father of a great nation
questions.explanation: God promised Abraham that he would be the father of a great nation and that all peoples on earth would be blessed through him (Genesis 12:2-3).

questions.question: What happened to Joseph after his brothers sold him?
options: He became a powerful leader in Egypt
questions.explanation: After being sold into slavery and put in prison, Joseph rose to become the second most powerful leader in Egypt (Genesis 41:41-43).

questions.question: How did God speak to Moses in the desert?
questions.explanation: God spoke to Moses from a burning bush that was on fire but did not burn up (Exodus 3:2-4).

questions.question: How did the walls of Jericho fall down?
options: The people marched, blew trumpets, and shouted as God commanded
questions.explanation: Joshua and the Israelites obeyed God by marching around the city and blowing trumpets. On the seventh day, they shouted and the walls fell flat (Joshua 6:20).

questions.question: Why did God choose David to be king?
options: Because God looked at his heart
questions.explanation: God told Samuel that He does not look at outward appearance but looks at the heart. David had a heart that loved God (1 Samuel 16:7).

questions.question: What did David use to defeat the giant Goliath?
questions.explanation: David used a sling and a single stone to defeat Goliath, trusting in God's power rather than human weapons (1 Samuel 17:49-50).
